majors.name: Electronic Engineering
majors.why: You study circuits and devices, so it's listed as a qualifying major in most postings for design, device, process, test and equipment roles.

majors.name: Electrical Engineering
majors.why: A major that almost always appears in postings for process and equipment roles and for fab power facilities.

majors.name: Semiconductor Engineering
majors.why: Where it's offered as its own program, it's named directly in postings for device, process, design, package and equipment roles, making it the most broadly applicable.

majors.name: Telecommunications Engineering
majors.why: Used in digital design, firmware and IT, and also leads into patent and equipment roles.

majors.name: Control & Instrumentation Engineering
majors.why: Control majors are listed separately in postings for equipment service, utilities and metrology.

majors.name: Nano & Optical Engineering
majors.why: A strength in lithography, photomasks and metrology. It's rarely named on its own in postings, so graduates apply widely to device and process roles too.

majors.name: Computer Engineering
majors.why: Listed as a qualifying major in postings for IT and software, design verification, test and production management.

majors.name: Software Engineering
majors.why: A good fit for software-centric roles such as fab automation, firmware and IT infrastructure.

majors.name: AI & Data Science
majors.why: Closest to roles that analyze yield and defect data. It pays to build semiconductor knowledge alongside.

majors.name: Information Security
majors.why: Leads straight into security roles that prevent technology leaks. Look at IT infrastructure too.

majors.name: Materials Science & Engineering
majors.why: A materials major almost always appears in postings for process, device, package and analysis roles.

majors.name: Chemical Engineering
majors.why: Listed broadly for process, equipment, package, chemical/gas and materials roles.

majors.name: Chemistry
majors.why: Appears in postings for process and materials development, analysis, chemicals and EHS.

majors.name: Polymer Engineering
majors.why: Used in materials R&D and package materials (resins, photosensitive materials).

majors.name: Energy Engineering
majors.why: Some chipmakers list energy majors in safety and infrastructure postings, and it also leads into materials roles.

majors.name: Environmental Engineering
majors.why: Appears in postings for fab environment and safety, and gas/chemical utilities.

majors.name: Mechanical Engineering
majors.why: The most widely requested major, spanning equipment service, equipment engineering, packaging and infrastructure.

majors.name: Mechatronics & Robotics
majors.why: Used in equipment installation and service, equipment R&D and automation.

majors.name: Industrial Engineering
majors.why: Industrial engineering is listed separately in postings for production management, IT, equipment and infrastructure.

majors.name: Safety Engineering
majors.why: Leads directly into fab safety and health and gas management.

majors.name: Architecture, Civil & Building Services
majors.why: Appears in postings for cleanroom and fab construction and facilities operation.

majors.name: Transportation Mechanical Engineering
majors.why: As a mechanical discipline, you can apply to equipment roles. It's rarely named on its own in postings.

majors.name: Physics
majors.why: Physics is often listed in postings for device, process and analysis roles.

majors.name: Mathematics
majors.why: Used in modeling, data and design algorithms. In postings' major requirements it's usually grouped as math/statistics.

majors.name: Statistics
majors.why: Appears in postings for production management, yield, quality and data analysis.

majors.name: Business Administration
majors.why: Appears in postings for business support, production management, sales and marketing, and product planning.

majors.name: Economics & International Trade
majors.why: Used in sales, planning and business support.

majors.name: Accounting & Finance
majors.why: Directly used in business support roles such as finance, procurement and HR.

majors.name: Law & Intellectual Property
majors.why: Patent postings center on STEM majors. Law helps as a double major and also leads into contracts and business support.

majors.name: Languages & International Studies
majors.why: Language skills are an edge in sales and equipment support for customers in other countries. Technical roles still assume a STEM major.
